name: large_vs_mid_cap_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: The intraday return spread between NIFTY 50 (large cap) and NIFTY Midcap 100 reflects shifting risk appetite. When mid-caps outperform large-caps early in the day (risk-on), the spread tends to mean-revert in the afternoon as profit-taking and risk-reduction flows dominate. Conversely, when large-caps outperform (risk-off), the spread reverts as bargain hunters enter mid-caps. This pattern exists because: (1) institutional flows hit large-caps first (more liquid) creating a lead-lag, (2) retail traders pile into mid-caps with a delay (checking social media, WhatsApp tip groups), (3) end-of-day risk reduction favors exiting mid-caps first. The reversion is incomplete (30-50% of the peak spread) but reliable.
universe: NIFTY 50 liquid names + NIFTY Midcap 100 liquid names
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 proxy: NIFTY 50 ETF or top 5 by weight. Midcap proxy: top 5 NIFTY Midcap 100 by ADV (>₹20 crore)

other: FII/DII cash market net buy/sell data (available by 09:30 next day for calibration)

conditions: spread_zscore > 1.5 (large-caps outperforming, mid-caps lagging — expect mid-cap catch-up)
midcap_volume_ratio > 0.7 (mid-caps still actively traded, not abandoned)
long.confirmation: spread_zscore starts declining from peak (crosses below 1.3 from above 1.5)

conditions: spread_zscore < -1.5 (mid-caps outperforming, large-caps lagging — expect large-cap catch-up)
short.confirmation: spread_zscore starts rising from trough (crosses above -1.3 from below -1.5)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation: long mid-cap proxy + short large-cap proxy (or vice versa)

exit.time_stop: exit by 15:00 if target not reached
exit.signal_exit: vix_level spikes > 22 during trade (regime change to risk-off)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; in high VIX, flight-to-quality means large-cap outperformance persists all day
filters.time_filter: no entries before 11:00 (need 1.75 hours of spread data) or after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: both NIFTY 50 and Midcap 100 trading at > 0.7x typical volume
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 |return| > 1.5% intraday (strong trend day, no reversion)
filters.spread_filter: individual stock bid-ask < 10 bps (mid-caps can be wider)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry, RBI policy, budget day
other_filters: skip if spread_zscore hasn't reached ±1.5 by 13:00 (insufficient divergence)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the large/mid-cap risk appetite rotation is a structural feature of Indian markets driven by persistent differences in investor composition (FIIs dominate large-cap, retail/DII dominate mid-cap).

weaknesses: Mid-cap stocks have wider bid-ask spreads and thinner liquidity, making the short leg (or long leg in mid-caps) more expensive to execute and exit.
On genuine risk-off days (global crisis, geopolitical events), large-caps keep outperforming all day and the spread never reverts — the stop loss at z-score ±2.5 gets hit.
Very low trade frequency (1-2/day) and long hold time (45-120 min) mean the strategy ties up capital with modest expected return per trade.
prior_art: Banz (1981) 'The Relationship Between Return and Market Value of Common Stocks' — size effect foundation. Hong, Lim & Stein (2000) on slow information diffusion in small/mid-cap stocks. In India, Agarwal (2012) studies size-based anomalies in NSE.
notes: The mid-cap leg should use a basket of 3-5 stocks to diversify idiosyncratic risk. Single-stock mid-cap positions are too volatile for a relative value strategy. NIFTY Midcap 100 futures (if available) would be ideal for the mid-cap leg.
